sentences.text:
?Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 14126 of 2023

Applicant :- Sawari Devi @ Samari Devi And Another
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thr.Its Sec. Home U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Laloo Yadav,Alind Kumar,Balwant Kumar Singh,Kiran Rani Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Laloo Yadav and Sri Balwant Kumar Singh, learned counsels for the applicants and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha, learned AGA for the State.
2.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicants on bail in Case Crime No. 0309 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 120B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Bhelupur,
District Varanasi during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 04.09.2022 through an application moved under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. dated 06.05.2022 and according to the FIR, the marriage of the daughter of the informant was performed with the son of applicants and after marriage applicants and other family members including husband of the deceased tortured the deceased for want of Rs. 5 lakhs and on 20.01.2022 at about 5.30 AM in the morning the wife of informant received a call from the mobile of deceased that condition of her daughter is quite serious and she has taken to Popular Hospital and when cousin brother of the daughter of the informant arrived at hospital then he found that daughter of the informant has died.

Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that entire allegation made against the applicants is totally false and baseless and applicants neither demanded any dowry nor they ever tortured the deceased and in fact deceased was having cyst on her chest and her treatment was going on in this regard and only due to the illness she died.
He further submits that entire medical prescription of the deceased has been annexed as Annexure-8 to the affidavit filed in support of present bail application.

He further submits that informant and his family members participated in the inquest proceedings, which was conducted in the presence of Ishwar Prasad Rawat, the cousin brother of the deceased and informant was also one of the Panch witness in the inquest dated 20.01.2022 but he did not make any allegation at that time against applicant and others and after about three and half months he moved an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and thereafter FIR of the present case was lodged and this fact clearly suggests that entire story narrated by the informant in the FIR is totally false and FIR has been lodged after due consultation on the legal advise.
He further submits that applicants are in-laws of the deceased and they were not having any concerned with the family affairs of the deceased and they resides in separate portion of the house.

5. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicants are in-laws of the deceased and there are allegation of demand of dowry and deceased died under abnormal circumstances within seven years of her marriage but he could not dispute the fact that FIR of the present case was lodged through an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and even application was moved after about three and half months and informant himself not only present during inquest proceeding but was also one of the Panch witness.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. Applicants are the parents of the husband of the deceased i.e. in-laws of the deceased and although deceased died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but it appears that FIR of the present case was lodged through an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and even application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved after about three and half months and informant of the case was present during inquest proceedings dated 20.01.2022 and he was also one of the Panch witness.
8.

Further, from the perusal of the Annexure-8, it appears that deceased was suffering from some diseases and she was under continuous medical treatment and her left chest cyst was diagnosed and on the basis of her medical prescription learned counsel for the applicant argued that she died due to her illness although as per post mortem report cause of death could not be ascertained

, therefore,
viscera was preserved but till date no viscera report is on record.
9.

Be that as it may, the fact that applicants are in-laws of the deceased and FIR of the present case was lodged after eight and half months on application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and even application under Section 156(3) was filed after three and half months, therefore, in my view,
applicants are entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

sentences.text: Let the applicants - Sawari Devi @ Samari Devi and Ghuran Prasad be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
( i) The applicants shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless their personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant sshall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicants.
